<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917575_theRebbe_481" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917575_theRebbe_481__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date for the maamar "Eileh Pekudei" for Shabbos Parshas Pekudei, 6 Adar Sheini, 5730.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B'Siyata D'Shmaya.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Pekudei,</t>
    <t s="2">6 Adar Sheini,</t>
    <t s="3">5730</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the textual difficulty of the double mention of "Mishkan" and the two interpretations of the phrase "asher pukad al pi Moshe."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"These are the accounts of the Mishkan, the Mishkan of Testimony, which were accounted at the mouth of Moshe..."</t>
    <t s="1">And the precise point of the phrase "the Mishkan, the Mishkan" twice is known.</t>
    <t s="2">Also, it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="3">that regarding the first Mishkan it says "Mishkan" simply, and regarding the second Mishkan it says "Mishkan of Testimony."</t>
    <t s="4">Also, it needs to be understood what is meant by "which were accounted at the mouth of Moshe,"</t>
    <t s="5">for there are two interpretations of this.</t>
    <t s="6">One, that it refers to what follows it,</t>
    <t s="7">to "Mishkan of Testimony."</t>
    <t s="8">Therefore it says "pukad" in the singular,</t>
    <t s="9">because only one Mishkan was accounted at the mouth of Moshe,</t>
    <t s="10">the aspect of the Mishkan of Testimony.</t>
    <t s="11">And another interpretation,</t>
    <t s="12">that "which were accounted at the mouth of Moshe" refers to the entire Mishkan,</t>
    <t s="13">also to the aspect of the simple Mishkan.</t>
    <t s="14">And on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="15">the simple interpretation</t>
    <t s="16">(for a verse does not depart from its simple meaning)</t>
    <t s="17">of "which were accounted at the mouth of Moshe" is that it refers to "These are the accounts of the Mishkan"</t>
    <t s="18">(that first it says "accounts" simply, and then it explains that this was at the mouth of Moshe).</t>
    <t s="19">And the connection between the two interpretations needs to be understood.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the two aspects of the Mishkan correspond to two levels of the Shechinah and two types of divine service, connecting them to mitzvos, teshuvah, and the service of tzaddikim.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And the point of the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="2">as it is brought in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="3">that the concept of the Mishkan is the indwelling of the Shechinah, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="4">"And they shall make Me a Sanctuary and I will dwell in their midst,"</t>
    <t s="5">and the two concepts in the Mishkan</t>
    <t s="6">[the simple Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony]</t>
    <t s="7">are two levels in the Shechinah,</t>
    <t s="8">the lower Shechinah and the upper Shechinah.</t>
    <t s="9">And according to the known principle that every Jew is a Mishkan and Sanctuary for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="10">[as our sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="11">on the verse</t>
    <t s="12">"And they shall make Me a Sanctuary and I will dwell in their midst,"</t>
    <t s="13">it does not say 'in its midst' but rather 'in their midst,'</t>
    <t s="14">within each and every Jew],</t>
    <t s="15">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="16">that the two concepts in the Mishkan</t>
    <t s="17">[the simple Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony]</t>
    <t s="18">are also in the Mishkan of Israel.</t>
    <t s="19">And according to the statement of our sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="20">on the verse "Mishkan of Testimony,"</t>
    <t s="21">"It is a testimony to all who come into the world that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired Israel,"</t>
    <t s="22">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="23">that this that Israel are a Mishkan</t>
    <t s="24">(simple)</t>
    <t s="25">is through the service of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="26">and this that they are a Mishkan of Testimony is through the service of teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="27">And this can be connected with what was brought above from Likkutei Torah, that the simple Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony are the lower Shechinah and the upper Shechinah,</t>
    <t s="28">for the lower Shechinah is Malchus and the upper Shechinah is Binah,</t>
    <t s="29">and correspondingly is the distinction between the service of Torah and mitzvos and the service of teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="30">that the fulfillment of mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="31">the mitzvos of the King,</t>
    <t s="32">is in Malchus,</t>
    <t s="33">and teshuvah is in Binah.</t>
    <t s="34">Also, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="35">that since the Mishkan</t>
    <t s="36">(the entire Mishkan)</t>
    <t s="37">was an atonement for the sin of the Golden Calf,</t>
    <t s="38">therefore,</t>
    <t s="39">even in the simple Mishkan the service of teshuvah is also included,</t>
    <t s="40">and the distinction between the simple Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony is,</t>
    <t s="41">that the simple Mishkan is lower teshuvah and the Mishkan of Testimony is upper teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="42">And this corresponds even more with what was brought above from Likkutei Torah, that the simple Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony are the lower Shechinah</t>
    <t s="43">(Malchus)</t>
    <t s="44">and the upper Shechinah</t>
    <t s="45">(Binah),</t>
    <t s="46">for lower teshuvah is the lower return of Hashem</t>
    <t s="47">(Malchus)</t>
    <t s="48">and upper teshuvah is the upper return of Hashem</t>
    <t s="49">(Binah).</t>
    <t s="50">And according to the opinion</t>
    <t s="51">that the command "And they shall make Me a Sanctuary" and also the donation for the Mishkan were before the sin of the Golden Calf,</t>
    <t s="52">when all of Israel were on the level of tzaddikim,</t>
    <t s="53">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="54">that the two aspects in the Mishkan</t>
    <t s="55">(the simple Mishkan and the Mishkan of Testimony)</t>
    <t s="56">are two aspects in the service of tzaddikim.</t>
    <t s="57">And as explained in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="58">that this that Israel are a simple Mishkan is through the fulfillment of positive commandments, and this that they are a Mishkan of Testimony is through the fulfillment of negative commandments.</t>
    <t s="59">And perhaps it can be said,</t>
    <t s="60">that the two concepts of the Mishkan in the service of tzaddikim are also in the service of the inner powers.</t>
    <t s="61">The simple Mishkan is the service of the heart,</t>
    <t s="62">and the Mishkan of Testimony is the service of the mind.</t>
    <t s="63">And this can be connected with what is explained in Likkutei Torah, that the two concepts of the Mishkan are positive and negative commandments,</t>
    <t s="64">for positive commandments are in Vav and Hei – the emotions</t>
    <t s="65">(Vav of Zeir Anpin,</t>
    <t s="66">and the final Hei – Malchus),</t>
    <t s="67">and negative commandments are in Yud and Hei – the intellect</t>
    <t s="68">(Yud – Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="69">Hei – Binah).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
